walkthroughs.body_html:
Irradiation: radiation reaches you but you are not radioactive afterwards.

Contamination: radioactive material gets on or inside you - keeps emitting.

Medical tracer: short half-life and gamma (penetrates, leaves quickly).

Smoke alarm: long half-life alpha (stops in air, lasts years).

Sources: radon, food, cosmic rays, medical.

Subtract from measurements to find true source activity.

mcqs.q: What absorber is needed to stop beta radiation?
options: A sheet of paper — beta is only slightly more penetrating than alpha.
A few millimetres of aluminium (or similar thin metal sheet).
It showed that alpha particles can pass through any material because they are massless.
Thick lead — only lead can stop any radiation.

mcqs.q: What did Rutherford's alpha-scattering experiment show about the atom?
options: It showed that atoms are solid spheres of positive charge with electrons embedded inside.
Beta radiation is most ionising because it consists of fast electrons.
Most of the atom is empty space, with a tiny dense positive nucleus.
It showed that alpha particles can pass through any material because they are massless.

mcqs.q: Which type of nuclear radiation is most ionising?
options: Thick lead — only lead can stop any radiation.
Gamma is most ionising because it can travel furthest and pass through almost anything.
Alpha radiation — large, doubly charged particles cause the most ionisation per unit distance.
Beta radiation is most ionising because it consists of fast electrons.
